tasks.title: Add AppState notify/router helper
tasks.description:
Creare un choke point unico per emissione notifiche, preferibilmente `AppState::notify`, evitando match manuali nei producer.

---
**Completion summary:**
SUPERSEDED by the T493 raise-path redesign — the single choke point exists, it is just not `AppState::notify`. Every notification goes through `Notification::…send()` (the public door) → the host-installed sink → `AppEvent::RaiseNotification` → `notification::raise(state, draft)` (heca/src/notification.rs), which is the ONE place `Instant::now()` is read and the only non-test caller of `NotificationRuntime::push`. tasks.title: Implement none notification mode
tasks.description:
Quando `notification_system = "none"`, sopprimere i producer non critici del piano senza sopprimere stderr/debug logs.

---
**Completion summary:**
SHIPPED (commit bfabbb7 / this session): `[settings.notification_system] mode = "none"` suppresses every notification. tasks.title: Define v1 behavior for system notification mode
tasks.description:
DECIDED (Antonio, 2026-08-28): the OS-notification backend is a ROUTING SINK behind Notification::send(), NOT a component.

THE MODEL:
- Notification::send() stays the only door. A producer never knows or cares where a notification surfaces — it types Notification::info("…").send() and nothing else.
- Where it surfaces is a host routing decision, invisible to the caller, driven by [settings.notification_system] mode:
  - "app"    → the in-app ToastStack (today's path via notification::raise → NotificationRuntime::push).
  - "system" → the OS backend (P063): macOS Notification Center, Linux libnotify, Windows toast. An OS notification has no bounds, no parent, no input — it is NOT a widget in heca's tree, which is exactly why it is a sink and not a component. Antonio's "place it anywhere and it handles itself" rule does not apply to it.
  - "none"   → dropped (already implemented — suppressed()).
- The routing happens in ONE place: notification::raise (heca/src/notification.rs), which already reads the mode. Today: App and System both fall through to the in-app store. P063 adds the System arm — raise() hands the accepted draft to an installed OS sink instead of / in addition to the store.
- The OS sink is installed the same way the in-app sink is (install_notification_sink pattern) — host-installed once at startup, absent in a headless test.

v1 BEHAVIOUR FOR "system" BEFORE P063 LANDS (this task):
- mode = "system" falls back to the in-app toast (App behaviour) — already the case.
- ADD a one-time info notification on the first raise under mode="system" while no OS sink is installed: "OS notifications aren't available yet — showing in-app." dedup_key "notification.system.unavailable" so it appears once, not per notification. This is the only code T222 itself ships; the rest is the P063 phase.

CONSEQUENCES for P063: it builds the OS sink + its install point + the raise() System arm + per-OS spikes. It does NOT build a component, a widget, a layer, or anything in the tree. Update the P063 phase description to this model.

CONSEQUENCE for T381: declined_actions lives in this same [settings.notification_system] table and assumes this routing model — build T381 after this is recorded (done) or alongside P063.

tasks.title: A declined action says so — the producer for "nothing happened, and here is why"
tasks.description:
A declined action — one that runs, finds a precondition unmet, and returns without doing anything — currently vanishes. From a held key that is fine; from the command palette, where the user picked the entry out of a list, it reads as a broken command. Reported 2026-07-30: "Move Column Up" chosen in the palette did nothing (handle_move_column_up, heca/src/handlers.rs, returns early when current_ws == 0). Same silent early return: move_column_down, move_pane_*, copy_selection (no selection), open_link_at_caret (no link), scrollback paging at an edge, and a Provider::perform that returns Handled::No.

=== AGREED DESIGN (Antonio, 2026-08-28) — reusable, centralised, no hardcoding, no per-action flags ===

1. PICKED vs BOUND. Every invocation carries a small tag, orthogonal to InteractionSource and invisible to ActionPolicy:
   - Picked = user chose it from an explicit list: command palette, right-click menu, a clicked button, RPC.
   - Bound = user pressed a key mapped to it.
   Set in the few dispatch entry points, never per action. NOTE: the palette today dispatches as InteractionSource::Keyboard on purpose (heca/src/chrome/palette.rs:318-352) so policy judges it like the key — keep that; the tag rides alongside, it does not replace the source.

2. ONE DECLINE OUTCOME at the single chokepoint. dispatch_action / route_interaction (heca/src/app/interaction.rs) already computes Blocked / NotRunnable / MissingArgs and throws them away for every caller but RPC. Add the handler case: a handler that early-returns calls cx.decline("already at the top") through a sink on the context it already has, instead of a bare return. A handler that does NOT call it produces no notification — safe default, and migration is incremental (wire the handlers people complain about; the rest stay silent exactly as today). Do NOT special-case the two column actions; do NOT change ~100 handler signatures.

3. SURFACING is decided centrally from the tag + config, never by the action:
   [settings.notification_system]
   declined_actions = "picked"   # "picked" (default) | "all" | "off"
   - "picked": a decline from palette/menu/RPC/button raises a toast; a keybinding decline stays silent. Fixes the reported bug with zero navigation spam.
   - "all": keybinding declines also notify (deduped — a held key is one toast, not a stream). Nav actions (focus_*, scroll_*, scrollback) decline constantly, which is why this is opt-in, not default.
   - "off": never.
   Config: add a NotificationDeclined enum to NotificationSystemConfig (heca-config/src/settings.rs), serde snake_case, default Picked; document in config.default.toml + README; thread to wherever the chokepoint reads it.

4. THE TOAST is built centrally from the DeclineReason + the action's catalog label/icon (ActionCatalog), low severity, no modal, no sound: Notification::info(format!("{label} — {reason}")).dedup_key(format!("declined:{action}")).send(). The dedup_key collapses any leaked spray.

DEFERRED, separate: prevention — an optional can_perform(action) -> bool so the palette renders an entry disabled (DropdownItem already has an `enabled` flag) rather than letting it be chosen and decline. That is palette work (was F003/P085/T358), not this task. This task is about telling the user what happened.

BEHAVIOURS TO PRESERVE: a decline is NOT an error — low severity, no sound, no modal. Holding a key at a list edge must not spray (dedup + the Bound-is-silent default both cover it).

tasks.title: Add name-keyed `notify` action — the raise capability
tasks.description:
Raising a notification today is `state.notifications.push(NotificationDraft, now)` (heca/src/notification.rs, ported from origin/feature/notification-system@ceade1e) — a private Rust method on AppState's store. No plugin, RPC caller, or keybinding can reach it; only dismiss (NotificationDismissOne/All/Last, P059) is a real registered action. This closes that asymmetry.

What exists to build on: `register_dynamic(registry, catalog, meta, handler)` at heca/src/actions.rs:418, `unregister_dynamic` at heca/src/actions.rs:471 — the name-keyed action path documented in docs/widgets.md:4863 "Registering a custom (name-keyed) action". AGENTS.md:1554 "Adding New Actions", the paragraph after step 11: a name-keyed action skips steps 1-4/8 (no WmAction variant, no action_from_name/build_action/priority/ActionRegistry::ALL descriptor).

Register `notify` via register_dynamic — NOT a WmAction variant. A future WASM plugin can only ever dispatch by name, never add an enum variant, and "any plugin can raise a notification" is the point of this action.

Declared args (ArgSpec, pattern at docs/widgets.md:4897):
- title: Text, required
- body: Text, optional
- severity: Enum (info|success|warning|danger), optional, default info
- dedup_key: Text, optional

Handler builds a NotificationDraft from the args (NotificationDraft::new(title).body(..).severity(..).dedup_key(..)) and calls state.notifications.push(draft, Instant::now()).

No action-button argument in v1 — deliberate scope, not a widget limitation: ToastSpec/ToastAction already support several typed actions per card (T487, landed on heca-4b's side), but there is no ArgKind for a nested Intent, so an RPC caller or a keybinding has no typed way to say "and run this other action with these args" as one argument value. A Rust-internal caller that wants a button uses NotificationDraft::action(label, intent) directly with a real Intent it already holds — unaffected by this task.

ActionPolicy: Global (app-level, no layout impact, must keep working while a floating pane is up) — cross-check against T213.

Edge cases: wire RPC parser support in heca/src/rpc.rs same as any other action; a default keybinding is optional (raising a static notification via keybinding is an unusual use case — command palette + RPC are the primary doors).

---
**Completion summary:**
SHIPPED: register_notify_action(registry, catalog) in heca/src/notification.rs, called once from HecaApp::resumed() in main.rs (after providers::register_provider_actions). Registered via register_dynamic — no WmAction variant. Args: title(Text,required)/body(Text,optional)/severity(Enum,optional,default info)/dedup_key(Text,optional). Handler builds a NotificationDraft and calls state.notifications.push. ActionPolicy::Global. Added NotificationSeverity: EnumArg+FromStr (accepts info/success/warning/danger/error) for the severity arg's declared vocabulary. CORRECTION to this task's own "edge cases" text: no rpc.rs changes needed — confirmed the generic `action <name> key=val` RPC verb (heca/src/rpc.rs parse_rpc) already reaches any declared action generically, built-in or name-keyed, with zero per-action code. No default keybinding, by design (command palette + RPC are the doors). VERIFICATION: cargo check -p heca clean. NOT verified: never actually invoked yet (no running app). FILES: heca/src/notification.rs, heca/src/main.rs.

### The raise architecture (P061/T493 — done)
`notification::raise(state, draft)` in `heca/src/notification.rs` is the ONE place `Instant::now()`
is read for a raised notification and the only non-test caller of `NotificationRuntime::push`. Both
doors converge on it: `Notification::…send()` (public builder → thread-local sink installed at
`heca/src/app/startup.rs` → `AppEvent::RaiseNotification` → `heca/src/main.rs`) and the name-keyed
`notify` action. `NotificationStore::push` + `NotificationRuntime::push` are `pub(crate)`;
`Notification` is the only public raise surface; `Notification::sticky()` is the auto-dismiss opt-out.

### Config — `[settings.notification_system]` (P061/T186/T187/T191 + T503 — done)
`heca-config/src/settings.rs`: `NotificationSystemConfig { mode: NotificationSystem, auto_dismiss_ms: u64 }`.
`mode = "app" | "system" | "none"` (default `App`): `none` → `raise()` early-returns via
`suppressed()`; `system` → in-app fallback + a one-time notice (`system_fallback_notice()`, T222).
`auto_dismiss_ms` (default 4000) applied at the runtime boundary in `push()` via
`NotificationLifecycle::with_auto_duration` — rewrites `Auto(_)`, leaves `Sticky`/explicit alone.
`set_auto_dismiss` / `set_mode` re-applied on `prefix+Shift+r` (`heca/src/main.rs`). Documented in
`config.default.toml` + `README.md` ("### Notifications").
**T503:** severity does NOT change lifetime — `default_lifetime_for_severity` was DELETED. Every
notification auto-dismisses; producers opt into persistence with `.sticky()`. **Reversible** if
Antonio wants errors sticky by default (re-add the severity→lifetime mapping in the draft setters).
